definition: Reluctant to speak or reveal one's thoughts.
example: The author was reticent about the experiences behind the novel.
nuance: Prefer reluctant for unwillingness to act; reticent precisely describes restraint in disclosure.
prompt: A colleague remains quiet about a sensitive personal subject.
options: Usually talkative, he became reticent when asked about his family.
She was reticent about the plan, explaining her reservations at great length.
The reticent runner hesitated to enter the race but freely discussed all his thoughts.
Everyone heard about his reticent promotion at yesterday's staff meeting.
reasons: This sentence demonstrates the meaning: reluctant to speak or reveal one's thoughts.
Openly explaining reservations at length is not being reserved in speech.
Reluctance to act alone is not reticence; the core meaning concerns speaking.
This mixes up reticent with recent; the word describes holding back speech, not timing.

practice.prompt: A food critic asks a chef to name the secret ingredient in her famous sauce.
options: The reticent chef recited every spice and measurement before the critic finished asking.
Annoyed by the question, the reticent chef shouted at the critic across the dining room.
The critic said the sauce was reticent of a stew his grandmother used to make.
The reticent chef only smiled and said the recipe would stay in her family.
reasons: Volunteering every detail eagerly is the opposite of keeping things to oneself.
Loud anger is not reticence; the word suggests quiet restraint, not hostility.
This confuses reticent with reminiscent; a sauce cannot recall a memory.
Politely declining to share what she knows shows she is holding back.
